subject: ss-pulmonology
title: Pleural effusion and pleural infection: Light criteria to drainage

steps.tx: The pleural space normally holds only a thin fluid film coupling lung to chest wall at roughly **minus 3 to minus 5** cmH2O. **Transudates** arise from systemic pressures such as heart failure, while **exudates** reflect local inflammation, infection or malignancy increasing capillary leak, and parietal lymphatics absorb up to **20 times** the formation rate.
steps.say: A thin film links lung to chest wall always in practice daily. Systemic pressure builds transudates in the chest daily in patients. Local inflammation builds exudates instead of transudates in practice.

steps.tx: Diagnostic **thoracentesis** separates transudate from exudate before further workup, since exudates demand cause hunting. **Light criteria** call an exudate when any one holds: fluid to serum protein above **0.5**, fluid to serum LDH above **0.6**, or fluid LDH above two thirds of the upper normal serum limit in absolute value.
steps.say: Thoracentesis separates transudate from exudate quite reliably in practice. Light criteria need only one positive test result in practice. Exudates then need cause hunting urgently in patients.

steps.tx: **Light criteria** misclassify about **25 percent** of transudates as exudates, the pseudoexudate problem after diuresis. A serum minus pleural protein gradient above **3.1 g/dL** or an albumin gradient above **1.2 g/dL** reclassifies these and works well in heart failure and hepatic hydrothorax patterns.
steps.say: A quarter of diuresed transudates look exudative always in practice. Gradients identify these cases in practice daily for clinicians. Albumin gradient above one point two works well in practice.

steps.tx: **Left ventricular failure** is the commonest pleural effusion cause worldwide as a transudate, with cirrhosis next in the United States pattern. **Hepatic hydrothorax** moves ascitic fluid through diaphragmatic defects into the chest and can develop spontaneous bacterial empyema, so asymmetry with ascites should prompt that specific search.
steps.say: Heart failure causes most transudates in clinical practice reported. Cirrhosis comes next in most series in practice daily. Hepatic hydrothorax allows ascites to enter the chest always in practice.

steps.tx: Exudate causes split into infection, **pulmonary embolism**, malignancy, and autoimmune or post surgical disease. Parapneumonic effusions reach up to **50 percent** of community pneumonias and constitute the commonest exudate, while malignancy accounts for roughly **75 percent** lung, breast and lymphoma cases, and embolism stays the most overlooked exudate cause.
steps.say: Infection, embolism and malignancy dominate exudates widely in practice. Half of pneumonias develop effusions in series reported daily. Embolism is often overlooked in practice daily in clinic.

steps.tx: Parapneumonic effusions evolve through exudative, fibrinopurulent and organising phases with pleural peel and trapped lung. Drainage is mandatory with loculated fluid, pus, positive Gram stain, **pH** below **7.20**, glucose below **60 mg/dL**, or LDH above **900 IU/L**, and about **10 percent** progress to frank empyema without early action.
steps.say: Parapneumonic phases are progressing toward empyema in patients daily. Low pH with pus requires drainage urgently in practice daily. About ten percent go on to empyema in pneumonia cases daily.

steps.tx: **Tuberculous pleuritis** is largely hypersensitivity to mycobacterial protein in the pleural space and yields a lymphocyte predominant exudate. **Adenosine deaminase** above **40 IU/L** or interferon gamma above **140 pg/mL** supports the diagnosis, while pleural biopsy culture yield exceeds fluid culture and adds pleural thickening on imaging.
steps.say: TB pleuritis gives lymphocyte rich exudates always in practice. Adenosine deaminase above forty supports TB disease in patients. Biopsy is better than fluid culture for diagnosis in practice daily.

steps.tx: Special fluid tests include triglycerides above **110 mg/dL** for **chylothorax** with milky appearance, haematocrit above half the blood value for **haemothorax**, **NT proBNP** above **1500 pg/mL** for cardiac origin, amylase for pancreatic or oesophageal disease, eosinophils for drug causation, and low glucose with rheumatoid disease. Malignant fluid gains from cytology and flow cytometry.
steps.say: Triglycerides above one hundred ten mark chyle clearly in practice. Haematocrit above half indicates blood in fluid daily in patients. NT proBNP above fifteen hundred marks cardiac origin in fluid.

steps.tx: Manage the cause first since transudates improve once heart failure or cirrhosis is treated, while complicated parapneumonic fluid with loculation, low **pH** or pus needs immediate tube drainage. Malignant effusions reflect disseminated disease with survival often under **6 months**, and recurrent effusions need pleural procedures rather than repeated taps alone for lasting relief.
steps.say: Treating the cause shrinks transudates over weeks in practice. Infected fluid needs prompt drainage in practice daily for patients. Malignant effusions signal disseminated disease stage in practice.

steps.tx: High yield anchors: Light protein ratio above **0.5** and LDH ratio above **0.6** define exudates, pseudoexudates misclassify about **25 percent**, gradients of **3.1** and **1.2 g/dL** rescue heart failure cases, parapneumonic fluid reaches **50 percent** of pneumonias with **10 percent** becoming empyema, drainage triggers at **pH 7.20**, glucose **60**, LDH **900**, **ADA** above **40**, triglyceride above **110**, **NT proBNP** above **1500**, and malignant survival often under **6 months**.
steps.say: Light cutoffs are zero point five and zero point six daily. Drainage triggers at pH seven point two daily in practice. Malignant effusions indicate poor survival ahead in patients.
